title: The Promise Hidden in a Photograph
fact_notes: 架空の教材例・思考実験。実在の調査、統計、法令、運用基準、実証結果ではない。登録台帳は制作来歴確認用。

sentences.en: At a fictional school, students organize a photography exhibition intended to celebrate the ordinary experiences of people who work in their neighborhood, including shopkeepers, delivery workers, and volunteers at a community center.
sentences.ja: 架空の学校で生徒は店主、配達員、地域センターのボランティアなど近隣で働く人々の日常を祝う写真展を企画する。

sentences.en: One student takes a portrait of a person repairing an old bicycle beside a small shop, after explaining that the picture will appear in an exhibition inside the school building.
sentences.ja: 一人の生徒は校内展示に写真が出ると説明したうえで小さな店のそばで古い自転車を修理する人の肖像写真を撮る。

sentences.en: The photograph is especially admired by the exhibition committee, and another student proposes using it on a publicly accessible website that will introduce the project to people in other communities.
sentences.ja: 写真は展示委員会に特に称賛され、他地域の人々に活動を紹介する公開ウェブサイトに使用することを別の生徒が提案する。

sentences.en: The original photographer hesitates because the person in the photograph agreed to a particular form of publication without being asked whether the picture could later be distributed to a potentially much wider audience.
sentences.ja: 写った人は特定形式での公開には同意したが後で潜在的にはるかに広い読者に配布してよいか聞かれていないため撮影者はためらう。

sentences.en: Members of the committee initially disagree about whether requesting further permission would be necessary, since the original photograph was taken openly and its subject had expressed enthusiasm for the planned school exhibition.
sentences.ja: 撮影は公然と行われ被写体も校内展示に熱意を示していたので追加許可を求める必要があるか当初委員は意見が分かれる。

sentences.en: Several students argue that the wider audience could appreciate the same positive aspects of the image, while others question whether the circumstances in which a photograph is encountered can influence the consequences of its publication.
sentences.ja: 広い読者も同じ肯定的側面を鑑賞できると主張する者もいれば、写真に出会う事情が公開の影響を左右するか疑問を持つ者もいる。

sentences.en: A person who is comfortable being recognized by members of a familiar community may have different expectations about appearing in a context that allows an image to be copied or shared beyond that community.
sentences.ja: 身近な共同体の人に認識されても平気な人が、その外で画像が複製・共有される文脈での露出には異なる期待を持つかもしれない。

sentences.en: The students recognize that enthusiasm for the original activity cannot automatically be interpreted as agreement to every subsequent use that someone else considers beneficial.
sentences.ja: 元の活動への熱意は他者が有益と考えるその後の全利用への同意と自動的には解釈できないと認識する。

sentences.en: The photographer returns to the shop and explains the proposed change, giving the subject an opportunity to consider how the photograph would be presented and who might be able to encounter it.
sentences.ja: 撮影者は店に戻り提案変更を説明し、写真の提示方法と誰が接触できるか考える機会を被写体に与える。

sentences.en: The person expresses a preference for keeping the original portrait within the school exhibition but offers to help the students prepare another image that does not show an identifiable face.
sentences.ja: 元の肖像は校内展示に留める希望を示すが識別可能な顔を写さない別画像の準備への協力を申し出る。

sentences.en: The students discuss how they could communicate the significance of the activity through a photograph of the person's hands and tools rather than assuming that public identification is essential to the project's purpose.
sentences.ja: 個人の公開特定が目的に不可欠と想定せず手や道具の写真で活動の意義を伝えられるか議論する。

sentences.en: They acknowledge that removing a face does not necessarily make a person anonymous, because other details in an image or its accompanying description may still allow someone to identify the subject.
sentences.ja: 顔を除けば必ず匿名になるとは限らず画像や説明の他の詳細で被写体を特定できる場合があると認める。

sentences.en: For the revised exhibition, the committee prepares a clear explanation of the intended audience and discusses how requests to use individual photographs outside the original project should be handled.
sentences.ja: 修正展に向け委員会は想定読者の明確な説明を作り個別写真を元の活動外で使用する依頼への対応を話し合う。

sentences.en: The students avoid claiming that their fictional conversation establishes the legal requirements for taking or publishing photographs in every actual situation, which may depend on rules and circumstances beyond the scope of the example.
sentences.ja: 架空会話が実際の全状況での撮影・公開の法的要件を確定するとは主張せず、それは例の範囲外の規則や事情に依存し得る。

sentences.en: Their aim is instead to examine the ethical significance of the expectations created when one person invites another to participate in a project.
sentences.ja: 目的はむしろ一人が他者を活動に招く際に生じた期待の倫理的重要性を吟味することだ。

sentences.en: An apparently minor modification to the way an image is distributed can alter the relationship between the person who supplied it and the organization responsible for its publication.
sentences.ja: 画像配布方法の一見小さな変更が画像を提供した人と公開担当組織の関係を変え得る。

sentences.en: Respecting someone's participation requires more than recognizing that an initial agreement was obtained before a project began.
sentences.ja: 人の参加を尊重するには活動開始前に初期同意を得たと認識する以上のことが必要だ。

sentences.en: It also requires attention to the particular conditions under which that agreement was made and to changes that could give the original decision a different practical significance.
sentences.ja: 合意時の特定条件と元の判断に異なる実務的意味を与え得る変更への注意も要する。

sentences.en: A worthwhile public purpose does not by itself demonstrate that every possible method of pursuing that purpose is equally appropriate.
sentences.ja: 価値ある公共目的だけでは追求方法が全て同等に適切と示さない。

sentences.en: The fictional exhibition illustrates how a creative project can preserve its intended message while reconsidering the means through which that message is communicated to a wider audience.
sentences.ja: 架空展は創造的活動が広い読者への伝達手段を再考しつつ意図したメッセージを保存できることを示す。

vocabulary.definition: in a way accessible to the public
able to be reached or used
not identified by name or identity
change made to suit a situation

questions.prompt: What had the photographed person originally agreed to?
options: Publishing the portrait on any future website.
Selling the image to a newspaper.
Displaying the portrait inside the school.

questions.prompt: Why did the photographer hesitate about the website?
options: The new distribution could exceed the original agreement.
The subject disliked the school exhibition.
The website could not display photographs.

questions.prompt: Why might a wider audience affect the subject's expectations?
options: The original photograph automatically becomes anonymous.
A public website has no viewers.
The image could be copied and shared in a different context.

questions.prompt: What did the students recognize about enthusiasm?
options: It does not imply agreement to all later uses.
It is necessary for every visitor to attend.
It proves every publication method is legal.
questions.explanation_ja: 初期熱意は包括同意でない。

options: Keep the original within the school and help create another image.
Remove all photographs from the project.
Publish the portrait on every site.
End all cooperation with the students.

questions.prompt: Why does removing a face not necessarily guarantee anonymity?
options: A photograph without a face always contains a name.
Other visual or descriptive details may identify the person.

questions.prompt: What is the aim of the fictional discussion?
options: Examine ethical expectations created through participation.
Prove every project must be publicly accessible.

questions.prompt: How might distribution change a relationship?
options: It always removes the original person's interests.
It makes the initial project meaningless.
It may alter the practical meaning of the original agreement.
questions.explanation_ja: 当初同意の意味の変化。

options: A positive purpose justifies every method of sharing.
Permission for one exhibition always permits wider distribution.
Creative projects should respect the scope of participants' agreements as publication plans change.
Responsible projects should avoid all photography.
questions.explanation_ja: 公開方法変更時の同意の範囲。

paraphrases.source: The original photographer hesitates because the person in the photograph agreed to a particular form of publication without being asked whether the picture could later be distributed to a potentially much wider audience.
paraphrases.rewrite: The person agreed to one exhibition but had not been asked about wider distribution.

paraphrases.source: Several students argue that the wider audience could appreciate the same positive aspects of the image, while others question whether the circumstances in which a photograph is encountered can influence the consequences of its publication.
paraphrases.rewrite: Some emphasize wider appreciation while others consider the consequences of a new context.

paraphrases.source: They acknowledge that removing a face does not necessarily make a person anonymous, because other details in an image or its accompanying description may still allow someone to identify the subject.
paraphrases.rewrite: A person may still be identifiable through details besides the face.

paraphrases.source: A worthwhile public purpose does not by itself demonstrate that every possible method of pursuing that purpose is equally appropriate.
paraphrases.rewrite: A valuable goal alone does not establish that every method is appropriate.

discourse.role_ja: 特定が必要との想定を避ける。
法的証明でなく倫理の考察。
初期同意に加え変更への注意。
